title: Fine-base affine log-ideal atlases and their canonical comparisons
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $P$ a commutative monoid with canonical group completion $G$, $\alpha:P\to A$, and $E\subset P$ finite. Use log structures, charts and geometric log stalks [def-trf-fs-log-blowup], the fine-log convention [def-trf-fine-log-etale-descent-datum], general log morphisms and the actual tensor chart rings $B_Q=A\otimes_{\mathbf Z[P]}\mathbf Z[Q]$ with coefficient and monomial maps [def-trf-log-ideal-chart-presentation, def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. Fix a log structure $M$ on $\operatorname{Spec}A$, a chart section $c:P\to M(\operatorname{Spec}A)$, a log scheme $(X,N)$ and log morphism $b:(X,N)\to(\operatorname{Spec}A,M)$. Given $Q_e\subset G$ and $i_e:P\to Q_e$ inducing the canonical inclusion into $G$ for $e\in E$, an affine log-ideal atlas consists of open immersions $j_e:\operatorname{Spec}B_{Q_e}\to X$ covering $X$ over the canonical maps to $\operatorname{Spec}A$, charts $Q_e\to N(\operatorname{Spec}B_{Q_e})$ associated to the canonical tensor monomials and compatible with $c$, and elements $d_{ef}\in Q_e$ equal in $G$ to $f/e$. Its exact pairwise intersections are $j_e(D(1\otimes z^{d_{ef}}))$, with the induced log identifications, and the pulled ideal generated by $E$ is generated by $e$ on the $e$-chart. Its generator-locus predicate says that at every geometric point membership in the $e$-chart is equivalent to divisibility of every generator by $e$ in the log stalk. A tensor ring map is normalized when it sends coefficients along the specified ring map and monomials along the specified monoid map. A comparison of two such atlases is a log morphism over the base with normalized inclusion maps on every chart, compatible log-chart maps and Cartesian chart squares [def-pc-fibre-product]. It is a finite comparison when the inverse image of each chart is exactly the corresponding chart, the morphism is finite, and every affine inverse image is affine with finite coordinate ring [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. A strict etale base-change presentation consists of an ordinary Cartesian log square with strict projection, an atlas for the changed coefficient ring and pulled chart, and normalized Cartesian chart squares. For $Q_e=\langle P,h/e:h\in E\rangle$ and its root saturation $Q_e^s$, a finite translate set $F\subset Q_e^s$ means $Q_e^s=\bigcup_{f\in F}fQ_e$; the spanning predicate means that such sets exist and, for every such $F$ and canonically normalized comparison, each element of $B_{Q_e^s}$ is a finite sum $\sum_{f\in F}a_f(1\otimes z^f)$ with $a_f\in B_{Q_e}$.

source.place: VIII 3.1.19, 3.3.5--3.3.9, printed pp. 101 and 107--108; finite translation presentation in VIII 3.2.9, finiteness sentence, printed p. 104.
